mainTopic: Contradicted witnesses: the מחלוקת of רב נחמן and רבא, whether a court may undo its own ruling, and the 'great authorities' רב נחמן relied on.
overview: The amud opens with רב נחמן's answer: the witnesses were contradicted only about the years of use, not about the land belonging to the claimant's ancestors. The גמרא asks whether רב נחמן and רבא are repeating the מחלוקת of רב הונא and רב חסדא about two groups of witnesses who contradict each other. It concludes that both follow רב הונא. רב נחמן trusts the witnesses even about the same matter, while רבא trusts them only in a different case. The land story then continues: the other man brings witnesses that the land was his ancestors', and רב נחמן rules that the court removes the man it placed there, without worrying about the court looking foolish. רבא, or רבי זעירא, objects from a ברייתא: a woman who remarried before contradicting witnesses came does not have to leave. רב נחמן first says he will not act, but then he does act, and the גמרא defends him as relying on great authorities. It brings the משנה about raising someone to כהונה with one witness, and starts asking how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differs from רבי אלעזר. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the ancestors part was never contradicted
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains why the witnesses are still believed about the ancestral ownership: nobody contradicted that part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the testimony contradicted about the ancestors?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן is answering the challenge from just before, that these witnesses were already contradicted. He points out that the other group only argued about who used the field. They never argued about whether it belonged to the claimant's ancestors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claimant's witnesses said two things: the land belonged to his ancestors, and he used it for the years of חזקה. Only the second part was contradicted. So רב נחמן says the first part still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Ancestors / fathers. Here it means the testimony that the land belonged to the claimant's family.
Was contradicted (from הַכְחָשָׁה)
Here it means 'Is it so that…?' It is a rhetorical question, not 'who'.

phrases.english: Was it contradicted regarding the ancestors?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב נחמן's ruling from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A contradiction about one part of the testimony (the use of the land) does not cancel the other part (the ancestral ownership).

steps.title: Is this an older מחלוקת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא and רב נחמן are really repeating the מחלוקת of רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבא and רב נחמן are arguing about the same thing that רב הונא and רב חסדא argued about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a link between the current מחלוקת and an earlier one. It is setting up a quote of that earlier מחלוקת, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לימא signals a suggestion the גמרא often goes on to reject. The idea is that this new case may just be one example of a general argument about witnesses who were contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion that is often rejected later.
A מחלוקת, a dispute
They are arguing

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rava and Rav Nachman

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא קָמִיפַּלְגִי?
phrases.english: are arguing in the dispute of Rav Huna and Rav Chisda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רבא and asks whether it matches an earlier מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רב נחמן / רבא מחלוקת the same as the רב הונא / רב חסדא מחלוקת?

steps.title: רב הונא and רב חסדא on contradicting witness groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier מחלוקת. רב הונא says each contradicting group may still testify on its own. רב חסדא says we do not use lying witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: when two groups of witnesses contradict each other, רב הונא says this group may come by itself and testify, and that group may come by itself and testify. רב חסדא says: why do I need these lying witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the earlier מחלוקת it just mentioned. Two groups of witnesses said opposite things, so one group must be lying, but we don't know which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says that since we can't tell who lied, each group is still allowed to testify in court. רב חסדא says that one of them surely lied, so we don't trust either group.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated. It introduces a מחלוקת of אמוראים.
Groups (sets) of witnesses
That contradict
Lying witnesses

phrases.english: As it was stated: two groups of witnesses
that contradict each other
Rav Huna said:
This group comes by itself and testifies,
and that group comes by itself and testifies.
And Rav Chisda said:
Why do I need these lying witnesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: שְׁתֵּי כִּתֵּי עֵדִים הַמַּכְחִישׁוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the earlier מחלוקת that step 2 mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: each contradicting group may still testify on its own. רב חסדא: neither group is trusted.

steps.title: Matching each אמורא to a side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the suggested match: רב נחמן follows רב הונא, and רבא follows רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב נחמן holds like רב הונא, and רבא holds like רב חסדא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes the suggestion exact by pairing each אמורא with one side of the earlier מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן still trusts the contradicted witnesses about the ancestors. That looks like רב הונא, who still trusts contradicted witnesses. רבא rejects them, which looks like רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Like רב הונא, following his opinion

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַב נַחְמָן – דְּאָמַר כְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Nachman says like Rav Huna,
and Rava like Rav Chisda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב נַחְמָן דְּאָמַר כְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מחלוקת quoted in step 3 to finish the suggestion from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב נחמן's view follow רב הונא, and רבא's view follow רב חסדא?

steps.title: According to רב חסדא, nobody would argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the match. If we followed רב חסדא, even רב נחמן would reject these witnesses, so the מחלוקת must be inside רב הונא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב חסדא, everyone agrees. When they argue, it is according to רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. It says the argument between רב נחמן and רבא cannot be about רב חסדא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא doesn't trust contradicted witnesses at all. So under his view, even רב נחמן would agree to throw out the ancestors testimony. That means רב נחמן and רבא must both hold like רב הונא and argue about how far his view goes.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Everyone
They do not argue

phrases.english: According to Rav Chisda,
everyone agrees,
when they argue, it is according to Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the match proposed in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבא follows רב חסדא; both רב נחמן and רבא work within רב הונא's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רב חסדא even רב נחמן would reject the witnesses, so his view cannot be one side of the מחלוקת.

steps.title: רבא: רב הונא only meant a different testimony
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן follows רב הונא fully. רבא says רב הונא only allowed contradicted witnesses to testify in a different case, not about the same matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן holds like רב הונא. And רבא says: רב הונא only said this for a different testimony, but not for the same testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא can agree with רב הונא and still reject the ancestors testimony. With this, it finishes its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא let each contradicted group testify again, but רבא says that means in another case. Here the ancestors testimony is about the same land as the contradicted testimony, so רבא does not accept it. רב נחמן applies רב הונא's view even to the same testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this far, meaning his ruling was limited to this case
A different testimony, a different case
The same testimony

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת of רב נחמן and רבא is NOT רב הונא against רב חסדא. Both follow רב הונא. רב נחמן trusts contradicted witnesses even about the same matter. רבא trusts them only in a different case.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא holds like רב חסדא. The גמרא's final answer puts רבא inside רב הונא's view, only limiting it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key idea: a witness group that was contradicted may still be fine for other cases, yet still be doubtful about the very matter where it was contradicted.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman holds like Rav Huna.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא – עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: And Rava: Rav Huna only said his ruling
for a different testimony,
but for the same testimony, no.
phrases.notes: Here 'the same testimony' means the ancestors testimony, since it is about the same land as the contradicted part.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אֶלָּא לְעֵדוּת אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 5 by showing how רב נחמן and רבא each read רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an earlier ruling (רב הונא) so that both אמוראים fit inside it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא rejects the witnesses because he holds like רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא agrees with רב הונא but limits him to a different testimony. רב נחמן applies רב הונא even to the same testimony.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רב נחמן and רבא follow רב הונא. They argue only about whether his ruling also covers the same testimony.

steps.title: The second claimant brings ancestral witnesses, and רב נחמן reverses the court's placement
steps.stepSummary: The second claimant now brings witnesses that the land belonged to his ancestors. רב נחמן rules that the court removes the man it had placed on the land, and is not worried about the court looking foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the other man brought witnesses that the land was his ancestors'. רב נחמן said: We put him onto the land, and we take him off. We are not worried that the court will look foolish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the land story from earlier on the דף. The man who first had only witnesses that he used the land now also brings witnesses that it was his ancestors'. רב נחמן reverses the court's earlier placement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, only one side had witnesses about the ancestors, so the court placed him on the land. Now both sides have such witnesses, and the evidence is balanced. רב נחמן says the court simply undoes its earlier step and does not worry about a זילותא דבי דינא.

keyTerms.meaning: We brought him down, and we bring him up. In other words, the court that put him on the land can take him off.
Making the court look foolish or unreliable by reversing itself.
Witnesses that the land belonged to his ancestors.
We are concerned or worried about something.

phrases.english: He then brought witnesses that it was his ancestors'.
Rav Nachman said: We brought him down onto the land,
and we bring him up off of it;
phrases.notes: Picture the court "lowering" someone onto a field to take it, and now "lifting" him back off.

phrases.english: we are not concerned about making the court look foolish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אֲנַן אַחֲתִינֵּיהּ, אֲנַן מַסְּקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion about contradicted witnesses (steps 2-6) to finish the land case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court may reverse its own earlier placement when new evidence comes. Worry about the court looking foolish is not a reason to stop it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the target of the objection that follows. That objection asks whether courts really undo actions already carried out.

steps.title: Objection from the case of a woman with contradicting witnesses about her husband
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or רבי זעירא, quotes a ברייתא. When two witnesses contradict two others about a husband's death or a divorce, the woman may not remarry. But if she did remarry, she does not leave. רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי says she must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא (some say רבי זעירא) objected from a ברייתא. Two witnesses say the husband died and two say he did not. Or two say she was divorced and two say she was not. She should not remarry, but if she did remarry, she does not have to leave. רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי says: she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן. This step lays out the ברייתא. The next step adds רבי מנחם's explanation, which makes the challenge sharp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first opinion says that once she has remarried, we do not undo it, even though the witnesses are evenly split. That clashes with רב נחמן, who was ready to undo the court's action once the evidence became balanced.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה.
And some say. It brings a second version of who said something.
She may not marry, at the start.
But if she already married, she does not have to leave her husband.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא says the woman is allowed to remarry. At the start she may not. The question is only what happens after she already did.

phrases.english: Rava objects, and some say it was Rabbi Zeira:
If two witnesses say: The husband died,
and two say: He did not die;
or two say: She was divorced,
and two say: She was not divorced –
this woman may not marry,
but if she married, she does not leave her new husband.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei says: She must leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the court removes the man it had placed on the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, once the woman has remarried on the basis of one pair of witnesses, the opposing pair does not undo it. So something already done should not be reversed because the evidence is now balanced.

steps.title: רבי מנחם limits his view, so everyone agrees a finished marriage stands
steps.stepSummary: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי explains that she must leave only if the contradicting witnesses came before she remarried. If they came after, even he agrees she stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי said: When do I say she must leave? When the witnesses came first and she married afterward. But if she married and the witnesses came afterward, she does not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי מנחם explaining his own opinion. This finishes רבא's objection and makes it stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both opinions in the ברייתא agree on one point. If the marriage happened first and the contradicting witnesses came later, we do not undo it. That is exactly רב נחמן's case: the court acted first and the new witnesses came later. Yet he did undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: When do I say this? It introduces a speaker limiting his own ruling.

keyTerms.term: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִשֵּׂאת
keyTerms.meaning: When the witnesses came first and she married afterward.
She married first and the witnesses came afterward.

steps.confusionAlert: The order of events is everything here. Witnesses first and then marriage means she leaves, according to רבי מנחם. Marriage first and then witnesses means everyone agrees she stays.

phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei said:
When do I say she must leave?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִשֵּׂאת;
phrases.english: When the witnesses came and afterward she married;
phrases.notes: These are the witnesses saying the husband is alive or she was not divorced. She married even though they had already testified.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִשֵּׂאת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים –
phrases.english: but if she married and afterward the witnesses came –
this woman does not leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵימָתַי אֲנִי אוֹמֵר תֵּצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 8 and sharpens the objection against רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the stricter opinion agrees that an action already taken is not undone by contradicting witnesses who come later. So no one in the ברייתא supports reversing the court's placement.

steps.title: רב נחמן accepts the objection and will not act on his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן admits he had planned to act on his ruling. Since רבא, and earlier רב המנונא in Syria, both challenged him, he will not carry it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: I had planned to carry this out in practice. Now that you challenged me, and רב המנונא also challenged me in Syria, I will not carry it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the objection by backing down. He does not offer a defense; he simply says he will not put his ruling into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate scholars raised the same kind of challenge, and that leads רב נחמן to say he will hold back. This is not where the story ends: the next step reports that he acted on his ruling after all.

keyTerms.meaning: To carry out a ruling in practice.
You raised an objection against me.
An אמורא who had already challenged רב נחמן on this point in Syria.
Syria.

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן first said a court can reverse its own action without worrying about looking foolish. After the objection from the ברייתא of the remarried woman, he said he would not act on it. The next step shows that in the end he did act, relying on great authorities.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא סְבַרִי לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא;
phrases.english: He said to him: I thought to carry out an action;
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן. The "action" is removing the man from the land, as he ruled in step 7.

phrases.english: now that you have raised an objection against me,
and Rav Hamnuna raised an objection against me in Syria –
I will not carry out an action in this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא סְבַרִי לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן responds to the objection of steps 8-9 by retracting in practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At this point רב נחמן says he will not put his reversal into practice because of the objections. The next step reports that he acted anyway, and the גמרא defends this as relying on a dispute among great authorities.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the surprise in the next step, where רב נחמן acts anyway and the גמרא explains why that was not a mistake.

steps.title: רב נחמן acts on his ruling after all
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן went out and carried out his ruling. People thought he had made a mistake. The גמרא says he did not; he relied on great authorities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן went out and acted on his ruling. Anyone who saw it thought he had made a mistake. But that is not so. He did it because the matter depends on a dispute among great authorities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב נחמן did act on his ruling after all. It defends him by saying the issue is argued over by great authorities, and it is getting ready to show us that argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רב נחמן said he would not act because רבא and רב המנונא challenged him. Here he acts anyway, and the גמרא explains that this was not careless. The question is a real dispute among great authorities, so he had solid opinions to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: He performed an action; he actually carried out the ruling
A mistake
Literally 'great ropes'; an issue that depends on great authorities

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying רב נחמן ignored his critics. It says the opposite of a mistake: he had great authorities on his side.

phrases.english: He went out and performed an action.
phrases.notes: He means רב נחמן actually took the land away, following his own ruling.

phrases.english: Whoever saw it thought:
It is a mistake on his part;
But it is not so,
rather, because it hangs on great ropes.
phrases.notes: Literally 'great ropes.' He means the question depends on a dispute between great authorities.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the plan in step 10: רב נחמן acts after all, and the גמרא defends him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן carried out his ruling because it rests on a dispute among great authorities.

steps.title: The משנה about raising someone to priesthood with one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי יהודה says one witness cannot make someone a כהן. רבי אלעזר says one witness is enough when no one challenges him. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, in the name of רבי שמעון בן הסגן, says one witness is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says we do not raise a person to כהונה based on one witness. רבי אלעזר said: When is that? When there are people challenging him. But when no one is challenging him, we do raise him to כהונה based on one witness. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי שמעון בן הסגן: We raise a person to כהונה based on one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show the 'great authorities' who disagree. This is the source behind the defense of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three opinions appear. רבי יהודה always needs two witnesses. רבי אלעזר allows one witness only if there are no challengers. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows one witness without mentioning any condition. The גמרא will now look closely at how these opinions differ.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
We raise someone to the status of a כהן
One witness
Challengers; people who dispute the claim
The deputy כהן גדול

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishnah:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
We do not raise a person to priesthood
based on one witness.
Rabbi Elazar said: When is this?
Where there are challengers,
but where there are no challengers,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלִין לַכְּהוּנָּה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד.
phrases.english: we raise a person to priesthood based on one witness.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon, son of the deputy High Priest:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלִין לַכְּהוּנָּה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד.
phrases.english: We raise a person to priesthood based on one witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the 'great authorities' mentioned in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן's ruling depends on a dispute among great authorities
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כתובות about raising someone to כהונה based on one witness

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to say the same as רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is listed separately, since his opinion looks the same as רבי אלעזר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is saying the same thing as רבי אלעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. If two opinions are listed separately, they should differ, but these two look identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both say one witness is enough to make someone a כהן. רבי אלעזר limits this to a case with no challengers, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל probably agrees when there are no challengers too. So the גמרא wants to know where they actually disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר!
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is the same as Rabbi Elazar!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinions of רבי אלעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions listed separately should differ, but both allow one witness, so they seem identical.

steps.title: Suggesting a difference: a challenge raised by one person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to suggest that the two opinions differ when only one person challenges. רבי אלעזר holds that a challenge from one person counts. The text stops in the middle of this suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that a challenge from one person is the difference between them: רבי אלעזר holds that a challenge from one person counts as a challenge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to step 13 by finding a case where the two might disagree. The sentence is still unfinished at the end of this amud and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the two argue about what happens when only one person objects. According to the suggestion, רבי אלעזר treats even one objector as a real challenge, so one witness would not be enough. The opening words 'and if you would say' hint that the גמרא may go on to question this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
A challenge raised by one person
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: The thought is not finished here. 'וכי תימא' introduces a suggestion, not the גמרא's final answer.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
a challenge by one person is the difference between them:
Rabbi Elazar holds: a challenge by one person

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא עַרְעָר חַד אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a case where the two opinions differ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seem to hold the same view.
